title: Speculative kernel merge exposes stale-cache window and precision divergence during interleaved prefill-decode
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
We observed rare correctness regressions after enabling speculative kernel merging (a perf optimization that coalesces adjacent kernels to reduce launch overhead). Failures present as: (1) token shifts from stale KV entries during long prefill + interleaved decode workloads, and (2) small numerical divergences (mixed-precision rounding) that amplify in downstream logits and cause sampling differences.

How it manifests:
- Probabilistic sample drift (not deterministic) on long-context generation with interleaved user requests.
- Reproducible with stressed interleaving (concurrent prefill on one stream while the scheduler merges kernels from a different workqueue).
- KV cache slot tags occasionally refer to an older slab window after a speculative merge completes during a prefill pipeline flush.

Reproduction steps (minimal harness):
1) Start runtime with kernel-merging enabled and kernel-scheduler: speculative-merge policy.
2) Feed a long prefill (2k tokens) on task A. During prefill flush, trigger many short decode requests on task B (1-4 tokens) to force scheduler interleave.
3) Use the attached reproducer script (link below) under AVX2 GPU emulation; failure observed ~1 in 600 runs on our CI stress runner.

Impact and urgency:
- High: affects correctness of serving outputs for some production workloads with interleaved multi-tenant patterns.
- Regression introduced by a perf optimization; must either fix correctness or gate the optimization behind safe heuristics.

Investigation notes so far (timeline):
- 2025-02-12: Initial alert from canary -> PR triage. Priority escalated due to customer-facing divergence for a mid-market customer using long-context chat.
- 2025-02-14: Triage run: captured traces showing kernel merge event overlapped with prefill KV flush. Observed stale-cache reads with sequence-number mismatch.
- 2025-02-16: Added deterministic instrumentation: per-slot sequence counters + merge-event logs. Confirmed that speculative merge can complete and reassign buffers before prefill flush completes, leaving transient stale views.
- 2025-02-20: Hypothesis validated: race between speculative-merge finalization (which reclaims/repurposes slab segments) and prefill write-back leads to stale reads that get interpreted as valid KV entries.

Root cause hypothesis:
- The speculative merge path reuses slab segments without properly synchronizing with outstanding prefill state machines. Because merge reduces the number of kernel invocations and coalesces writes, one side-effect is tighter timing windows on slab reuse. The prefill state machine can observe slot metadata that appears valid (non-zero length) but whose backing buffer was recycled and partially overwritten by the merged kernel path.
- Mixed-precision reorderings inside the merged kernel also alter accumulation order, producing subtle fp rounding differences that amplify across attention and cause downstream token probability drift.

Proposed mitigations and tradeoffs:
Option A (short-term, safe):
- Disable speculative kernel merging when prefill sequences are active or when multi-stream interleaving exceeds a threshold.
- Cost: measurable perf regression under the specific mode (approx +4-7% median latencies on 1-token bursts in our synthetic benchmark).

Option B (medium-term, correct):
- Introduce sequence-numbered KV-slot fencing: every slot write increments a fence counter; readers validate fence after memory barrier. Ensure merge finalization waits for in-flight prefill fences.
- Add explicit memory barriers and a merge finalization handshake to avoid reuse until all prefill state machines ack.
- Cost: complexity increase; some perf overhead but can be tuned (estimated +1-2% latency).

Option C (long-term, performant):
- Rework speculative merging logic to keep per-stream slot ownership metadata rather than blind slab reuse, enabling zero-cost correctness checks at read time.
- Cost: larger engineering effort but keeps most perf wins.

Immediate plan (agreed by on-call + runtime owners):
1) Ship short-term safeguard (Option A) behind a config flag and enable automatically for canary/production for affected customers. Branch: PR #9876.
2) Implement medium-term fence-based fix (Option B) and add unit+stress tests. Target runtime-1.21.
3) Instrument canary and dashboards with merge-event, fence misses, and KV-validate metrics.
4) Run extended perf regression and correctness stress for 72h across regions.

Acceptance criteria:
- No stale-cache read reproductions on CI reproducer after patch for 1M stress iterations.
- Canary with production traffic (selected customer) shows no divergence for 48h.
- Automated tests added to kernel-scheduler unit tests and end-to-end prefill-decode stress harness.
- PR passes design/eng review and is rolled with a toggle.

Links and artifacts:
- Reproducer harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-tests/tree/main/repro/speculative-merge-stress
- PR (short-term safeguard): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9876
- Kernel scheduler design notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/kernel-scheduler/speculative-merge
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/merge-events/merge-canary

Notes on telemetry to add:
- metric.runtime.merge.finalize_latency_ms (histogram)
- metric.runtime.kv.read_validation_failures (counter, tags: stream_id, slot_id)
- trace span: kernel.merge.finalize -> includes slab_id, seq_before, seq_after

Risks and roll-back plan:
- Rolling out short-term disable increases request median latency slightly; rollback by re-enabling speculative merge if perf/regression unacceptable for a customer (but then we will re-schedule for tracked customers only).
- If fence-based fix affects throughput, we will canary with limited capacity and revert under controlled window.
